- slice=minimal: code genuinely does ONLY the small slice, and its test checks ONLY that slice. E.g. - slice=single: author to final form minus later-feature parts, per construct. Removal commits ('refactor!: remove ...') delete the named subsystem.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- csr-transport-bringup: Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). # Build the user-facing andesim runtime library into build/runtime/:
#
#   libandesim_runtime.a   trap.o handler.o vplat_syscalls.o
#   crt0.o                   startfile; kept OUTSIDE the archive because
#                            nothing references _start, so the linker
#                            would never extract it from a .a (same
#                            reason toolchains ship crt0.o next to libc.a)
#   andesim.ld             linker script (load base 0x00100000)
#   include/andesim/ROI.h  ROI markers (HINT NOPs; same dir rides -B)
#
# Users link with:
#   gcc ... -B <repo>/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs hello.c
# or, without the gcc driver:
#   gcc ... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T andesim.ld crt0.o hello.c \
#       -L <repo>/build/runtime \
#       -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
#
# Toolchain location comes from config.env (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN), same as
# tests/fixtures/Makefile.
TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain)
endif

TRIPLE := riscv64-unknown-elf
CC := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/$(TRIPLE)-gcc
AR := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/$(TRIPLE)-ar

# rv64gc objects link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the RISC-V arch
# attributes), so one build serves both -march variants.
CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

OUT ?= ../build/runtime
LIB_OBJS := $(OUT)/trap.o $(OUT)/handler.o $(OUT)/vplat_syscalls.o

.PHONY: all clean

all: $(OUT)/libandesim_runtime.a $(OUT)/crt0.o $(OUT)/andesim.ld \
     $(OUT)/andesim.specs $(OUT)/include/andesim/ROI.h

$(OUT):

$(OUT)/%.o: %.S | $(OUT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(OUT)/%.o: %.c | $(OUT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(OUT)/trap.o: core_v5.h

$(OUT)/libandesim_runtime.a: $(LIB_OBJS)

$(OUT)/andesim.ld: andesim.ld | $(OUT)

content.content:
1 # Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
   2 #
   3 # Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
   4 # `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
   5 # command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
   6 # to bypass the env var.
   7 
   8 TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
   9 ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
  10 $(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
  11 endif
  12 CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
  13 LD        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
  14 OBJDUMP   := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump
  15 
  16 # Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
  17 # user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
  18 # script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
  19 RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
  20 LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
  21 # Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
  22 HELPERS_DIR := runtime
  23 
  24 CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
  25 LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static
  26 
  27 # All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
  28 RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_all_fprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
  29                rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
  30                rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
  31                rt_m_ext_trigcause rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode
  32 
  33 # Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
  34 # NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
  35 # Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
  36 BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
  37                   break_verify_diverge
  38 
  39 # C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
  40 # through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
  41 # same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
  42 # -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
  43 # artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
  44 # the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
  45 # andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
  46 # vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
  47 # the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
  48 # ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
  49 RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
  50                     rt_c_fcsr
  51 RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
  52 RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file
  53 
  54 RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
  55                    $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
  56 # Prereqs of the runtime grouped target -- the runtime sources.
  57 RUNTIME_DEPS    := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
  58                    $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
  59                    $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
  60 VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
  61 VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
  62                 $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
  63                 $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
  64 VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
  65 # RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
  66 # link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
  67 # The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
  68 VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
  69 
  70 .PHONY: all clean dump
  71 
  72 all: spin.elf handoff_exit.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
  73      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
  74      $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
  75      $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)
  76 
  77 # Note: handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are legacy (referenced only
  78 # by EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp). They still build for completeness
  79 # but are not in active CTest. All targets now share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.
  80 
  81 spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
  82     $(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
  83     $(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@
  84 
  85 handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S $(LDSCRIPT)
  86     $(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
  87     $(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@
  88 
  89 handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
  90     $(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
  91     $(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@
  92 
  93 $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
  94     $(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
  95     $(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
  96 
  97 # Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
  98 # (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
  99 $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
 100     $(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
 101     $(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
 102 
 103 # C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
 104 # above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
 105 $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
 106     $(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
 107       -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
 108 
 109 # RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
 110 # changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
 111 $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
 112     $(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
 113       -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
 114 
 115 # vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
 116 # features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
 117 $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
 118     $(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
 119 
 120 # One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
 121 $(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
 122     $(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)
 123 
 124 # Markerless GEMM twin. Explicit rule, NOT in RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the
 125 # pattern rule would look for a nonexistent rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same
 126 # source, same link as the marked V fixtures, plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS
 127 # (drops the ROI marker HINTs) so pc-mode and marker-mode measure the
 128 # same GEMM kernel.
 129 rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
 130     $(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
 131       -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@
 132 
 133 dump: spin.elf handoff_exit.elf
 134     $(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
 135     $(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf
 136 
 137 clean:
 138     rm -f spin.o spin.elf handoff_exit.o handoff_exit.elf \
 139           handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
 140           $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
 141           $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
 142           rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
 143           $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)
